compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered by the Step 7 sibling sweep while fixing `downy-feminist-leopard` (1d1b-a719-b675-4a1f), which enumerated `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` in a new `EDGE_PATHS` detect manifest so an edge change is at least signalled (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=nginx_edge_manual`).

The **same silent-drift class** still affects the HOST-nginx *includes* the edge template glob-includes, which are materialized by `compose-up.sh` at boot — NOT by the autodeploy loop:

- `infra/scripts/materialize-opcert-guard.sh` — writes `/etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf` (the fail-closed `/opcert/` guard map) + reloads nginx. Invoked only by `compose-up.sh`.
- `infra/scripts/materialize-mcp-upstream.sh` — installs the committed `infra/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` seed into `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` (only-if-absent) + reloads nginx. Invoked only by `compose-up.sh`.
- `infra/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` — the committed seed itself (after first boot the live include is blue-green managed by autodeploy; a change to the seed never re-reaches the box).
- `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` — the boot orchestrator itself.

None of these appears in ANY autodeploy path manifest (BOT_PATHS, SECRETS_PATHS, MCP_PATHS, CONFIG_PATHS, OBS_PATHS, CERTBOT_PATHS, and now EDGE_PATHS). `autodeploy.sh` re-runs `install-observability.sh` / `install-certbot-timer.sh` / `fetch-secrets.sh` on their manifest deltas, but it never re-runs `compose-up.sh` or the two `materialize-*.sh` host-nginx materializers. So a merged change to any of their *sources* rsyncs to `/opt/rebar` and then silently does nothing — the exact drift class OBS_PATHS/CERTBOT_PATHS (and now EDGE_PATHS) were created to fix.

## Evidence

- `grep -n "materialize-opcert-guard\|materialize-mcp-upstream\|compose-up" infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` → no invocation; these are absent from every manifest.
- `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` invokes `materialize-opcert-guard.sh` and `materialize-mcp-upstream.sh`; `autodeploy.sh` never invokes `compose-up.sh`.
- Both materialize scripts perform `nginx -s reload` (host-nginx apply), which is exactly the deferred v1→v2 boundary (ADR 0079).

## Why NOT fixed in the parent (1d1b)

Out of scope for `downy-feminist-leopard` (operator-approved Option A: detect-and-signal for the edge *template* only). This class is distinct: (1) applying it means re-running an infra/ script that calls `nginx -s reload` (the deferred v2 auto-apply boundary), and (2) it is a different surface (compose-up materializers), not the edge template. It also is NOT covered by epic `sprucing-wise-dikkops` (6d60), which is scoped to full auto-apply of the edge *template* (render → nginx -t → reload → rollback).

## Suggested disposition

Decide per input whether it wants (a) DETECT-ONLY signal parity (a manifest + an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` block, mirroring EDGE_PATHS/CONFIG_PATHS — safe, no reload), or (b) apply/re-materialize parity (add to a manifest and re-run the idempotent materializer, like OBS_PATHS/CERTBOT_PATHS — but these reload nginx, so that decision must respect the v1→v2 apply boundary). `compose-up.sh` may belong to the provisioning layer (like `install-autodeploy.sh`, which is deliberately excluded) rather than the autodeploy loop; confirm before enumerating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of `materialize-opcert-guard.sh`, `materialize-mcp-upstream.sh`, the `mcp-upstream.conf` seed, and `compose-up.sh` is either enumerated in an autodeploy manifest (detect-signal or apply, per the decision above) or explicitly documented as intentionally excluded (like `install-autodeploy.sh`), so no host-nginx materializer can drift silently.
- [ ] Any apply path respects the ADR 0079 v1→v2 boundary (no unattended `nginx -s reload` beyond what is already sanctioned).
- [ ] Regression coverage mirroring `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py` for any newly-signalled input.
compiled_state.title: Autodeploy never detects source changes to compose-up's host-nginx materializers (materialize-opcert-guard.sh, materialize-mcp-upstream.sh, mcp-upstream.conf seed) — same silent-drift class as the nginx edge template
